title: Never Too Late to Run
intro: You are going to read about a woman who ran her first marathon at the age of 58.

passage: Three years ago, Nodira Rashidova could not run for a bus. She was 55, she worked in an office in Tashkent, and she spent most of her free time on the sofa. "I was always tired," she says. "I had no energy, even in the morning." Then her doctor told her something important: she needed to move more, or she was going to have serious health problems.

Nodira started slowly. On the first day, she walked around her neighbourhood for twenty minutes. After two weeks, she tried to run between two lamp posts. "My legs hurt and my face was red," she laughs. "But the next day I ran to the third lamp post." After six months, she could run five kilometres without stopping.

Then her daughter showed her a video of a marathon in Berlin. A marathon is a race of 42 kilometres. "That's crazy," Nodira said. But the idea stayed in her head. She joined a running club and found a coach, a young man called Aziz. He gave her a plan: three short runs and one long run every week. He also taught her to stretch before and after training, because tight muscles often cause an injury.

The training was not always easy. In winter, Nodira ran in the dark before work. Once she hurt her knee and had to stop for a month. "I cried a lot that month," she says. "But Aziz said, 'Your goal is still there. It can wait for you.'" Slowly, the distance of her long runs grew: 15 kilometres, then 25, then 32.

Last October, at the age of 58, Nodira finished her first marathon. It took her five hours and ten minutes. She was one of the last runners, but she did not care. "When I crossed the finish line, I felt so proud," she says. Today she is fit and healthy, and she sleeps well. Her next plan? "A marathon in Berlin, of course!"
